attempts: Attempt 1: DELETE /items/:id without Authorization header - deletes item and returns 204 instead of 401 unauthorized
Attempt 2: DELETE /items/:id with wrong Bearer token - deletes item and returns 204 instead of 401 unauthorized
Attempt 3: DELETE /items/:id with malformed Authorization header (bare token, no Bearer scheme) - deletes item and returns 204 instead of 401 unauthorized
Attempt 4: DELETE /items/999 without auth on non-existent item - returns 404 instead of 401, leaking existence via wrong error code

findings.claim: Authorization check is completely missing from DELETE /items/:id route; the implementation skips directly to id validation without validating the Authorization header against process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN
findings.evidence: Manual testing shows DELETE /items/:id succeeds with status 204 (deletes item) when sent without Authorization header, with wrong token, and with malformed Authorization header. Spec requires all three cases to return 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} per AC-3, AC-4, AC-5. No bearer token parsing, no process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN comparison, no 401 response logic present in the route handler.

findings.claim: Authorization is checked after id validation instead of before, violating spec requirement that auth failure takes precedence over id/existence checks
findings.evidence: DELETE /items/999 (non-existent id) without Authorization header returns 404 instead of 401. Spec AC-13 explicitly requires this scenario to return 401 to avoid leaking existence info to unauthenticated callers. Current code checks id format at line 54-56 before any auth logic exists, then checks item existence at line 58-60, guaranteeing 404 responses leak to unauthenticated users.

findings.claim: Bearer token parsing logic is absent; the route does not parse Authorization header for 'Bearer <token>' format with case-insensitive scheme and case-sensitive token
findings.evidence: No req.headers.authorization access, no regex/split to extract Bearer scheme and token, no case-insensitive scheme comparison (Bearer/bearer/BEARER all accepted per AC-6), no case-sensitive token match against process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN (AC-7 requires S3CRET to fail when token is s3cret). Manual testing shows Bearer, bearer, and BEARER headers all treated identically to missing headers - all allow deletion.

findings.claim: process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN is never read or validated; the route does not enforce that unset or empty ADMIN_TOKEN rejects all requests with 401
findings.evidence: Per AC-8 and AC-9, any request must return 401 when ADMIN_TOKEN is undefined or empty string. No process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN access in route handler. Manual test with ADMIN_TOKEN unset still allows deletion (status 204). Route has no early return based on env var state.

findings.claim: Six authorization-specific test cases fail because the implementation lacks auth logic, proving non-conformance with spec acceptance criteria AC-3, AC-4, AC-5, AC-7, AC-8, AC-9, AC-13
findings.evidence: Test suite shows failures: AC-3 expects 401 gets 204; AC-4 expects 401 gets 204; AC-5 (malformed headers) expects 401 gets 204; AC-7 (case-sensitive token) expects 401 gets 204; AC-8 (unset token) expects 401 gets 204; AC-9 (empty token) expects 401 gets 204; AC-13 (auth before id validation on empty store) expects 401 gets 404. These failures directly map to missing bearer token validation and env var checking in the route implementation.

Send DELETE /items/1 with Authorization: Bearer wrong-token → gets 204 instead of required 401, token verification completely absent
Send DELETE /items/999 (nonexistent) with no Authorization header → gets 404 instead of required 401, leaking item existence to unauthenticated users because auth is not checked first

findings.claim: DELETE /items/:id endpoint missing entire authorization layer - no Authorization header validation, no ADMIN_TOKEN check, no Bearer token parsing or verification
findings.evidence: The DELETE handler skips directly to ID validation at line 54 without any code that reads req.headers.authorization or process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN. Tests 6-12 all fail with status 204 returned for requests that should return 401. Examples: AC-3 (no header gets 204), AC-4 (wrong token gets 204), AC-7 (case-sensitive token not checked).

findings.claim: ID validation and existence check performed before authorization check, leaking item existence to unauthenticated users
findings.evidence: Lines 54-60 validate the ID format and check item existence without first verifying Authorization header. Spec requires 'Auth failure takes precedence over id validation and over item existence'. AC-13 test fails: DELETE /items/999 with no auth returns 404 (revealing item doesn't exist) instead of 401 (auth required first). Test output shows 'expected 401 actual 404'.

findings.claim: No token validation against process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN; Bearer scheme not validated as case-insensitive; token not validated as case-sensitive string
findings.evidence: Implementation lacks the token parsing logic. Spec design decision: 'Authorization header must be Bearer scheme (case-insensitive) followed by exactly one space and token (case-sensitive, compared with ===)'. Tests verify this: AC-5 fails for malformed headers (s3cret, Basic s3cret, Bearer with 2 spaces, etc. all get 204 instead of 401), AC-7 fails for case-sensitive token (S3CRET gets 204 instead of 401), AC-8/AC-9 fail for unset/empty ADMIN_TOKEN (should always reject, but deletion succeeds).

attempts: Attempt 1: Send DELETE /items/1 without Authorization header. Expected 401 {error: unauthorized}, received 204 — route accepts unauthenticated deletion.

Attempt 3: Send DELETE /items/1 with ADMIN_TOKEN unset and no Authorization header. Expected 401 {error: unauthorized}, received 204 — route ignores missing ADMIN_TOKEN requirement.

Attempt 5: Send DELETE /items/1 with Authorization: Bearer S3CRET when ADMIN_TOKEN=s3cret. Expected 401 (case-sensitive token), received 204 — token comparison not implemented.

findings.claim: Authorization check not prioritized over ID validation; leaks information about item existence to unauthenticated callers

findings.claim: No parsing or validation of Authorization header format; does not extract or verify Bearer token scheme or token value
findings.evidence: Implementation contains no code to read Authorization header, parse Bearer scheme, extract token, or compare against process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN. Test AC-5 sends malformed headers ('s3cret', 'Basic s3cret', 'Bearer ', 'Bearer  s3cret', etc.) and all receive 204 instead of 401.

findings.claim: Does not validate process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN as configured; accepts DELETE requests when ADMIN_TOKEN is unset or empty string
findings.evidence: Implementation never checks if ADMIN_TOKEN exists or is non-empty. Test AC-8 (ADMIN_TOKEN unset) and AC-9 (ADMIN_TOKEN empty string) both return 204 instead of 401. Spec requires that unset or empty ADMIN_TOKEN means 'no admin configured' → always reject with 401.

findings.claim: Token comparison not case-sensitive; no string equality check (===) against process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN
findings.evidence: Test AC-7 sends Authorization: Bearer S3CRET when process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN='s3cret' and receives 204 instead of 401. Spec requires exact string equality comparison (===) for token; this is critical for security.
